newsitem.title: CHILE: Blizzard traps more than 200 people in Andes.
newsitem.headline: Blizzard traps more than 200 people in Andes.

text.p: Attempts to rescue more than 200 people stranded at a border post high in the Andes were foiled on Sunday by a blizzard but Chilean airforce helicopters got out 29 people before the weather closed in, police said.
"We managed to bring 29 people down from the complex before the flights had to be suspended when it started snowing heavily," said police spokesman commander Mario Gonzalez.
"When the weather improves, we will rescue the people who are still up there."
Authorities said a total of 198 people, including seven children, remained trapped since Thursday at the immigration office at Los Libertadores border station on the Chilean-Argentine frontier.

Some 42 people have also been stranded at a refuge near the entrance of the Cristo Redentor tunnel linking the two countries after the vehicles in which they were traveling were trapped in the tunnel by Thursday's blizzard, officials said.
The 42 were well and had enough food for the next two days, Ximena Navasal, spokesman for the National Emergency Office, said.
Helicopters left more food and fuel at Los Libertadores, the main crossing point between the two countries, for those people who were not taken to safety.
The authorities will attempt a second helicopter rescue on Monday -- provided the weather clears, Navasal said.
"We will start the rescue again tomorrow at 7 a.m. (1100 GMT) if the conditions allow it," she said.
Police had to abandon Sunday's rescue mission involving three aircraft after just two hours because of heavy snow, high winds and poor visibility.
The storms, which have lashed the country for over a week, have dumped up to 20 feet (six meters) of snow in the Andes and caused serious flooding in central Chile.
The floods have killed 17 people, made several thousand homeless and left vast tracts of countryside under water.
Television images showed police on horseback and soldiers in amphibious craft rescuing people from isolated houses and farms surrounded by flooded fields.
The unusually heavy rainfall follows the worst drought in central Chile this century.
